question: A 24-year-old woman with HIV infection comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She has been inconsistently taking combined antiretroviral therapy for the past 5 years. She did not receive any childhood vaccinations because her parents were against them. During the consultation, the patient says that she wants to catch up on the missed vaccinations. Laboratory studies show a CD4+ T lymphocyte cell count of 180/mm3. Administration of the vaccine against which of the following agents should be avoided in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: HIV infection -> compromised immune system -> decreased ability to mount an effective immune response -> uncertainty in vaccine efficacy -> 70% confident CHAIN: CD4+ T lymphocyte count of 180/mm3 -> severe immunosuppression -> increased risk of vaccine-related complications -> avoid live vaccines -> 90% confident CHAIN: Inconsistent antiretroviral therapy -> suboptimal viral suppression -> impaired immune function -> increased risk of adverse vaccine reactions -> 80% confident CHAIN: Missed childhood vaccinations -> lack of immunity -> susceptibility to vaccine-preventable diseases -> need for catch-up vaccinations -> 80% confident CHAIN: Parents against childhood vaccinations -> missed vaccinations -> increased susceptibility to vaccine-preventable diseases -> 70%
analysis: In a patient with HIV infection and a low CD4+ T lymphocyte cell count, live vaccines should be avoided due to the risk of vaccine-induced disease. Varicella zoster virus vaccine is a live vaccine and should be avoided in this patient.
